reminder.notes:
## Bug fixes

- **Fixed repeating reminders firing years before their start date.** A reminder set for a date in the future with a repeat rule — "check the car battery, 1 April 2029, every day" — rang the next morning, and every morning after that. The start date was read, passed to the repeat logic, and then ignored by every rule except intervals, so daily, weekly, monthly and yearly all counted from today and the chosen date only ever set the time of day.

- **Every reminder now takes over the screen, whatever its priority.** Normal reminders arrived as a quiet notification in the tray that was easy to miss entirely — and a missed reminder is indistinguishable from a broken one. Priority now decides how insistent the alert is and whether it survives quiet hours, never whether you are interrupted at all.

  This needed the notification channel to be recreated. Android fixes a channel's importance when it first makes it and ignores every later change, so raising it in the app alone would have shipped a fix that did nothing on any phone that already had Reminder installed.

- **Location reminders now leave a trace in the diagnostics log.** Every other part of the app records what it did — scheduling, syncing, alarms, the watchdog — and geofencing recorded nothing, so "location reminders don't work" produced a log in which location was the one thing invisible. It now says whether a place was registered, or refused for want of "Allow all the time" location, or rejected by Play services and why.

## Features

- **New app icon.** The old one was a six-colour gradient bell on a white tile: nothing held its shape at the size a launcher actually draws, and the white tile disappeared into light wallpapers. It is now a single bell on the app's indigo, legible small.

## Notes

- If location reminders are not firing, the usual cause is Location permission set to "While using the app". Android will not deliver a place alert without **Allow all the time**, and the app refuses to save a location reminder without it rather than creating one that silently never fires.

mirrordrive.notes:
# Mirror v0.15.0

### Features
- App renamed "Mirror" (from "MirrorDrive"/"Mirror Drive") in the launcher, app title, and app-store listing. Package id and OAuth client are unchanged, so this update installs normally over the existing app.
- Mapping backup now lives in Drive's hidden App Data folder, one file per device install, so the same Google account signed into two phones can no longer have one phone's auto-backup silently overwrite the other's saved mappings.
- A restore picker (Settings, or offered automatically right after a fresh sign-in with no local mappings) lists every device's backup under the account and lets you choose which one to restore.
- Mapping backup now saves automatically on every add/edit/delete, not just when manually tapping "Back up" in Settings.
- Optional fleet diagnostics reporting (Settings > Troubleshooting): sends sanitized failure and background-sync delivery signals to help diagnose device-specific issues remotely. Off by default; never sends mapping paths, file names, or account details.
- Removed the "beta" label from the app-store listing and the in-app sign-in screen.

### Bug fixes
- Google Sign-In on release builds no longer fails right after install (the v0.14.0 signing-key rotation needed its new SHA-1 registered on the OAuth client; done).
- Mapping backups now actually persist across an uninstall/reinstall. Previously the backup/restore mechanism existed but was never triggered automatically, so a reinstall lost every mapping.

family.notes:
**Pre-release.** Under active development — do not rely on it as your only safety measure.

Installs over 0.9.1 and later normally. Coming from **0.8.0 or older, uninstall first** — those were signed with a different key.

## Features

### You can ask a child to share
Tap a child and choose **Ask them to share**. Their phone shows the request, and they can **Allow** or say **Not now**. Allowing sends their position straight away and starts sharing, so you can follow rather than being handed one dot that is already out of date.

Nothing starts until they agree. You can stop sharing at any time; only they can start it. That is the whole point — nobody in this family gets followed without saying yes first.

### Everyone is told apart at a glance
Each child now has their own colour and initials, on the map pin, on the accuracy circle and in the list. With more than one child sharing, three "Recent" pins used to be three identical dots and the only way to tell them apart was to read the labels on top of each other.

The colour belongs to the person, not to their place in the list, so nobody changes colour when a sibling joins or stops sharing.

### Your own position on the map
A plain "You" dot, so you can see where a child is relative to you instead of working it out from street names. **Your location is never uploaded and never shared with anyone** — it is drawn on your phone and stays there.

### Directions to a child
Opens your usual maps app, routed to where they are now. A route cannot follow someone who is moving, so reopen it to catch up — the app says so rather than pretending otherwise.

## Bug fixes

- **The refresh button now behaves like a button.** It spins while it is actually working and tells you when it has finished. Before, it did nothing visible at all: a slow connection, a dead one and a successful refresh looked exactly the same.

## Notes

- A child sees a request while the app is open. If their phone has it closed they will see it next time they open it — alerts for this are the next thing to add.

## Verified before publishing

`flutter analyze` clean, 215 tests passing, APK signed with the usual release key and aligned.

taashclub.notes:
Taash Club 1.1.0 - Playable 3-2-5 vs Computer, and Rules You Can Argue With

### Features
- Rules page for every game, reached from the game card in the lobby. Teen Patti, Rummy and 3-2-5 each get their deal, their rankings or contracts, and the house rules a table can vary.
- Feedback on any individual rule. If a rule is wrong, unclear, or simply not how your family plays, say so on that rule itself. Notes written offline are kept on the device and sent when you are next online, so a disagreement at the table is never lost.
- Solo play against the computer now works for Teen Do Paanch (3-2-5): kaat is called, all ten tricks are played out, and the deal is settled against the 3-2-5 contracts.
- Solo play against the computer now works for Rummy: draw from either pile, discard, drop, and declare, with the computer players drawing, discarding and declaring for themselves. If the cards run out before anyone declares, the deal is settled on the lowest count.

### Bug fixes
- Fixed 3-2-5 against the computer freezing immediately after the deal. The table appeared, cards were visible, and nothing further happened: the opening turn belonged to a computer player that was never asked to move.
- Fixed Rummy against the computer dealing a hand and then ignoring every tap. Drawing, discarding, dropping and declaring all did nothing, because only Teen Patti had an offline engine behind it.
- Fixed the 3-2-5 deck keeping one red and one black seven regardless of the table's house rule. It now keeps the pair the table actually chose, matching the server.
- Fixed the 3-2-5 setting for sevens describing the opposite of what it does. "Keep the black sevens" in fact removed them; the option now names what is removed and which pair is left in play.
- Fixed Teen Patti wild-card hands being scored differently depending on the order the cards were dealt. An Ace-low run built with a wild could be read as a pair, so the same three cards could win or lose.

### Notes for existing players
- This release is signed with a new key. Android will not install it over version 1.0.1, so uninstall the old app first and then install this one. Chips, profile and history live on the server and are restored when you sign in again.
